## Lectures (2 total)

- Lecture 1: Quality control of raw Illumina reads
- Lecture 2: Illumina read trimming and adapter clipping

*Note:* in a previous version of the course we used Trimmomatic to trim Illumina reads (which is why it's mentioned in the lectures). However, in your hands-on activity you will use **fastp** — both tools are similar and accomplish virtually the same thing, but fastp is *way* faster.

## Practical readings (3 total)

- [FastQC's official help pages](https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/Help) — not pretty, but very useful (click the links within the directories to read about each analysis/component of FastQC).
- [FastQC explained](https://hbctraining.github.io/Intro-to-rnaseq-hpc-salmon/lessons/qc_fastqc_assessment.html) — focuses on RNA-seq but still relevant; much nicer to read/look at than the official FastQC help pages.
- [FastQC results explained with pretty pictures](https://nf-co.re/eager/2.1.0/docs/output) — you only need to read the section titled "FastQC". Focuses on ancient DNA but does a great job explaining FastQC output and how to interpret it.

## Supplemental readings (optional, 1 total)

- Chen, et al. 2018. *fastp: an ultra-fast all-in-one FASTQ preprocessor*. <https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/34/17/i884/5093234>
